name: Proactive-Reactive Control Mode and Architectural Predictability
higher_order_principle: Predictable environments enable proactive control (sustained lateral PFC, anticipatory goal maintenance, metabolically steady). Unpredictable environments force reactive control (transient ACC conflict detection, stimulus-driven retrieval, metabolically bursty). Populations with reduced proactive capacity bear disproportionate cost in unpredictable buildings.
transferable_to: healthcare design (predictable layouts for cognitively impaired)
workplace design (open-plan interruption forcing reactive mode)
wayfinding systems (clear signage enabling proactive planning)
scope_conditions: Applies to environments requiring sustained goal-directed behavior
Proactive mode requires intact PFC and sufficient WM capacity
Predictability assessed at architectural scale (layout, signage)

interactions.description: T44 involves level of control; T45 involves temporal mode of control.
Chronic reactive mode leads to allostatic overload (bursty metabolic spikes).
T45 refines T38: same complexity causes different load profile depending on mode.

key_references: Braver, T. S. (2012). The variable nature of cognitive control. Trends in Cognitive Sciences.
Botvinick, M., & Cohen, J. D. (2014). The computational and neural basis of cognitive control.
